facts.fact_text: On 17 October 2003 the applicants took part in an anti-war demonstration in Istanbul.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, fifty to sixty persons, including the applicants, gathered in a square in Istanbul at 7.45 p.m.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the persons gathered in the square in Istanbul chanted anti-war slogans.

According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the persons gathered in the square were protesting against the Government's proposals to send soldiers to participate in the invasion of Iraq.
The applicants were arrested by police officers during the dispersal of the anti-war demonstration in Istanbul on 17 October 2003.
The applicants were taken into police custody following their arrest on 17 October 2003.
The applicants remained in police custody until their release the day following their arrest on 17 October 2003, i.e. on 18 October 2003.

On 21 October 2003 criminal proceedings were instigated against the applicants for having taken part in an unlawful demonstration, in breach of sections 33, 36 and 40 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police warned the gathered persons using loudspeakers that they were disturbing the flow of traffic.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police asked the gathered persons to disperse but were unsuccessful.

According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, when the police attempted to arrest some of the demonstrators and put them into police vehicles, a number of the demonstrators displayed rowdy behaviour.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police had to use force against a number of the demonstrators who displayed rowdy behaviour.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, a total of six persons, including the applicants, were arrested and taken to a police station at 8.30 p.m. on 17 October 2003.
The incident report of 17 October 2003 was signed by six police officers who were referred to in the report only by their identification numbers.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the first applicant had bruising on her lower lip.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the first applicant had bruising on her lower right leg.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the fourth applicant had bruising on the left side of his lower back.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the fourth applicant had bruising on the back of his right ear.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the fourth applicant's legs were sensitive.
According to the medical reports drawn up on 17 October 2003, the fourth applicant had redness in his left eye.

In deciding to close the investigation on 14 April 2004, the Bakırköy prosecutor considered, on the basis of the documents in the file, that when the applicants refused to disperse the police had had to use force against them.
The Bakırköy prosecutor concluded that the applicants' simple injuries had been caused when the police were exercising their statutory powers on the use of force.
On 21 October 2003 the Bakırköy prosecutor asked for an investigation to be opened into the applicants' allegations of ill-treatment.
The applicants submitted a formal complaint to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003.
The third applicant, Mr Hacı Badem, did not complain of ill-treatment in the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003.
The first applicant complained of ill-treatment in the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003.
The second applicant complained of ill-treatment in the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003.
The fourth applicant complained of ill-treatment in the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003.

In the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003, the first, second, and fourth applicants stated, referring to Article 3 of the Convention, that police officers had punched and kicked them in the course of their arrests on 17 October 2003.

In the formal complaint submitted to the Bakırköy prosecutor on 5 November 2003, the first, second, and fourth applicants stated, referring to Article 3 of the Convention, that police officers had punched and kicked them during their detention at the police station.
Between 10 December 2003 and 13 April 2004, the Bakırköy prosecutor questioned eleven police officers.
Ten of the eleven police officers questioned by the Bakırköy prosecutor denied having been at the demonstration on 17 October 2003.

Ten of the eleven police officers questioned by the Bakırköy prosecutor stated they had not seen any of the demonstrators because they had been working elsewhere at the time of the demonstration on 17 October 2003.
Police chief M.T. told the Bakırköy prosecutor that he had not taken part in the dispersal of the demonstration on 17 October 2003.
Police chief M.T. told the Bakırköy prosecutor that he had questioned the applicants in police custody.
Police chief M.T. denied having ill-treated any of the arrestees.
Police chief M.T. denied having sworn at any of the arrestees.
On 14 April 2004 the Bakırköy prosecutor decided to close the investigation into the applicants' allegations of ill-treatment.
The applicants lodged an objection against the Bakırköy prosecutor's decision of 14 April 2004 to close the investigation into their allegations of ill-treatment.
The Eyüp Assize Court rejected the applicants' objection against the Bakırköy prosecutor's decision to close the investigation on 8 December 2004.
The Eyüp Assize Court's decision of 8 December 2004 stated that it was to be served on the applicants.
According to a hand-written note on the Eyüp Assize Court's decision of 8 December 2004, the decision was communicated to the applicants on 9 February 2005.
